identity.what_it_is: A 7-mile (11 km) beach in Carmarthen Bay, south Wales, Welsh name Traeth Pentywyn, famous as the site of five world land speed record attempts between 1924 and 1927.
identity.where: Carmarthenshire, south Wales, stretching from Gilman Point in the west to Laugharne Sands (per Wikipedia) / Ginst Point (per Pendine Community Council) in the east; the village of Pendine sits at its western end.
identity.warnings: Beach (Pendine Sands) and village (Pendine, pop. 346 in 2011) are distinct entities and must not be conflated. No confirmed duplicate/near-duplicate 'Pendine' place exists elsewhere in the UK.

spike_candidates.statement: Parry-Thomas's car Babs was buried in the Pendine dunes after his fatal 1927 crash, exhumed 42 years later in 1969, and restored over the next 16 years.
spike_candidates.tension: Officialdom tried to erase the tragedy outright (seats slashed, dials smashed, car buried on inquest instruction) yet the beach's own buried wreck became its most beloved tourist icon four decades on.

spike_candidates.statement: The beach synonymous with speed and freedom is majority-owned by the Ministry of Defence, closed to the public most weekdays 8am-4.30pm, and driving on it today costs £2,000/day with prior permission.
spike_candidates.tension: A place mythologised as the ultimate open, flat expanse of freedom is, in practice, a fenced military range for most of the working week.

spike_candidates.statement: In just three years (1924-1927), Campbell and Parry-Thomas traded the land speed record four times at Pendine, ending when Parry-Thomas died trying to reclaim a record Campbell had retaken weeks earlier.
spike_candidates.tension: The record duel reads as friendly rivalry in tourism copy, but it was a compressed, fatal escalation that ended the era of British beach-based land speed racing at Pendine entirely.

facts.fact: Pendine Sands is a 7-mile (11 km) beach on Carmarthen Bay, Wales, known in Welsh as Traeth Pentywyn.
facts.quote: pendine sands ( welsh : traeth pentywyn ) is a 7-mile (11 km) beach on the shores of carmarthen bay on the south coast of wales . it stretches west to east from gilman point to laugharne sands.

facts.fact: The village of Pendine (Welsh: Pentywyn, 'end of the dunes') had a population of 346 at the 2011 census.
facts.quote: the population at the 2011 census was 346

facts.fact: Malcolm Campbell set the first Pendine land speed record on 25 September 1924 at 146.16 mph in the Sunbeam 350HP car 'Blue Bird'.
facts.quote: on 25 september 1924 he set a world land speed record of 146.16 mph (235.22 km/h) on pendine sands in his sunbeam 350hp car blue bird .

facts.fact: In April 1926 Parry-Thomas broke Campbell's record, reaching 171.02 mph in Babs.
facts.quote: in april 1926, parry-thomas added approximately 20 mph to break the land speed record at 171.02 mph (273.6 km/h) .

facts.fact: Campbell retook the record in February 1927 at 174.22 mph in his second Blue Bird.
facts.quote: campbell raised the record to 174.22 mph (280.38 km/h) in february 1927 with his second blue bird .

facts.fact: On 3 March 1927, Parry-Thomas crashed at about 170 mph attempting to reclaim the record from Campbell and was the first driver killed pursuing the land speed record.
facts.quote: on 3 march 1927, parry-thomas attempted to beat campbell's record. on his final run while travelling at about 170 mph (270 km/h) the car crashed.

facts.fact: After the inquest, Babs's seats were slashed, its dial glass smashed, and the wrecked car was buried in the Pendine dunes.
facts.quote: following the inquest into thomas's death, babs' s seats were slashed, the glass in the dials smashed, and the car was buried in the sand dunes at pendine .

facts.fact: Owen Wyn Owen, an engineering lecturer, excavated and restored Babs after it had lain buried on the tidal beach for decades.
facts.quote: his most famous restoration project, which received worldwide attention, was to excavate and restore babs , after 40 years buried on a tidal beach .

facts.fact: A final planned land speed attempt at Pendine ended when Giulio Foresti's car 'Djelmo' crashed and was destroyed during a test run on 26 November 1927.
facts.quote: one further attempt at the land speed record was planned by giulio foresti in the "djelmo", but foresti crashed during a test run on 26 november 1927, totally destroying the car.

facts.fact: In 1933 Amy Johnson and her husband Jim Mollison took off from Pendine Sands attempting a non-stop flight to New York in a de Havilland Dragon Rapide named 'Seafarer'.
facts.quote: in 1933, amy johnson and her husband, jim mollison , took off from pendine sands in a de havilland dragon rapide , g-accv "seafarer", to fly non-stop to new york.

facts.fact: Johnson and Mollison's aircraft ran out of fuel and crash-landed at Bridgeport, Connecticut, just short of New York, seriously injuring both.
facts.quote: their aircraft ran out of fuel and was forced to crash-land at bridgeport, connecticut , just short of new york; both were seriously injured in the crash.

facts.fact: In June 2000 Don Wales, grandson of Malcolm Campbell, set the UK electric land speed record at Pendine in Bluebird Electric 2, at 137 mph.
facts.quote: grandson of sir malcolm campbell and a nephew of donald campbell , set the uk electric land speed record at pendine sands in blue bird electric 2 , achieving a speed of 137 mph (220 km/h)

facts.fact: The Ministry of Defence acquired Pendine Sands during the Second World War and used it as a firing range.
facts.quote: the ministry of defence (mod) acquired pendine sands during the second world war and used it as a firing range .

facts.fact: All vehicles were banned from Pendine between 9 July 2004 and May 2010 on safety grounds; cars have been allowed back since May 2010.
facts.quote: between 9 july 2004 and may 2010 all vehicles were banned from using pendine because of safety concerns, but since may 2010 cars have again been allowed access .

facts.fact: In 2011 Aardman Animations built the world's largest stop-motion film set on the beach for the short film 'Gulp'.
facts.quote: in 2011, aardman animations claimed the world's largest stop motion film set for gulp , a short film .

facts.fact: The Vintage Hot Rod Association's inaugural amateur hot rod races were held at Pendine on 7 September 2013, timing 80 pre-1949 hot rods.
facts.quote: the vintage hot rod association hosted their inaugural amateur hot rod races on pendine sands on 7 september 2013. racing was open to members of the vhra and their pre-1949 hot rods and saw 80 vehicles being timed flat out on the sands.

facts.fact: In September 2013, Guy Martin set the UK speed record for a bicycle ridden in a vehicle's slipstream, hitting 112.9 mph behind a modified truck driven by Dave Jenkins.
facts.quote: in september 2013, guy martin broke the uk speed record for a bicycle ridden in the slipstream of another vehicle .

facts.fact: On 7 May 2015 actor Idris Elba broke the historic 'Flying Mile' UK land speed record in a Bentley Continental GT Speed, recording 180.361 mph.
facts.quote: on 7 may 2015, actor idris elba broke the historic 'flying mile' uk land speed record, originally set by malcolm campbell , in a bentley continental gt speed . the recorded speed was 180.361 mph .

facts.fact: On 21 July 2015, the 90th anniversary of Campbell's first Pendine record was marked by grandson Don Wales driving the restored Blue Bird at Pendine.
facts.quote: on 21 july 2015, at pendine beach, the 90th anniversary of sir malcolm campbell's first world land speed record in "blue bird" was recreated by his grandson, don wales, also a land speed record holder, in the fully restored car .

facts.fact: On 12 May 2018 a home-built car nicknamed the 'wooden shed' (an Audi RS4 engine in a wood-clad frame) set a new speed record of 101 mph at Pendine.
facts.quote: on 12 may 2018, a home-built 'wooden shed' (using an audi rs4 twin turbo engine, installed in a metal frame with wooden shed cladding) set a new speed record, achieving 101 mph (163 km/h) , breaking its own previous record of 80 mph (130 km/h) .

facts.fact: The next day, 13 May 2018, Zef Eisenberg set a new sand speed record of 201.5 mph on a Suzuki Hayabusa motorcycle, the first time 200+ mph was reached at Pendine by a wheeled vehicle.
facts.quote: the following day, 45-year-old guernsey businessman zef eisenberg set a new land speed 'sand' record of 201.5 mph (324.3 km/h) on his 350-horsepower supercharged suzuki hayabusa motorcycle, the first time a speed in excess of 200 miles per hour had been achieved at pendine .

facts.fact: In 2019 Eisenberg set a new record of 210.332 mph at Pendine in a modified Porsche 911, breaking both the flying mile and flying quarter records on the same day.
facts.quote: in 2019, eisenberg set a new record of 210.332 mph (338.497 km/h) in a modified porsche 911 . he broke the records for flying mile and flying quarter on the same day .

facts.fact: Pendine Sands has been used as a filming location for BBC's Top Gear and the BBC Cymru drama Keeping Faith, starring Eve Myles.
facts.quote: pendine sands has been used as a location for filming, including bbc's top gear and the bbc cymru drama keeping faith , starring eve myles .

facts.fact: MOD Pendine's military range is operated by QinetiQ, has a land area of 20.5 km2 with 9 km of shoreline and an 18 km2 sea danger area, and includes three test tracks.
facts.quote: the range occupies 20.5 square kilometres (7.9 sq mi) with 9 kilometres (5.6 mi) of shoreline and a sea danger area of 18 square kilometres (6.9 sq mi) . the range includes three test tracks .

facts.fact: Pendine community covers 409 hectares (1.58 sq mi) and lies south of the Landsker Line, the linguistic boundary in south Wales.
facts.quote: lies a few miles south of the linguistic boundary known as the landsker line , and is predominantly english-speaking .

facts.fact: Welsh-speaking in Pendine community rose from 13.9% in 2001 to 18.2% at the 2011 census.
facts.quote: the 2011 census showed 18.2% of the population could speak welsh , a rise from 13.9% in 2001.

facts.fact: Marros-Pendine Coast, a Site of Special Scientific Interest covering part of Pendine Sands, was designated in 1988 and covers 2.5 km2.
facts.quote: marros-pendine coast is a site of special scientific interest in carmarthen & dinefwr , wales . it includes marros sands , morfabychan beach and part of pendine sands and some of the cliffs and slopes above them.

facts.fact: The Higham Special, later renamed Babs, was bought from Louis Zborowski's estate by Parry-Thomas for £125 and rebuilt with a 27-litre Liberty V12 aero-engine.
facts.quote: using a 450 hp (340 kw) v12 liberty aero engine of 27 litres capacity, with a gearbox and chain-drive from a pre-war blitzen benz , it was the largest capacity racing car ever to run at brooklands .

facts.fact: Pendine Community Council owns the beach section at the village end and to the west; the MOD (via QinetiQ) owns the majority to the east, usually closed to the public 8am-4.30pm on weekdays but open at weekends.
facts.quote: while pendine community council owns a section of the beach at the village end and to the west, the ministry of defence (qinetiq) own the majority to the east.
facts.source_title: Community and beach information - Pendine Community Council

facts.fact: Dogs are specifically excluded from the community-council-owned 'bathing area' of the beach between the two slipways.
facts.quote: dogs are specifically excluded from the central area of the community council owned beach between the two slipways.
facts.source_title: Community and beach information - Pendine Community Council

facts.fact: Launching a boat or jet ski at Pendine Sands requires membership of a club registered with Pendine Community Council.
facts.quote: you cannot launch a boat or jet ski at pendine sands unless you are a member of a club registered with pendine community council.
facts.source_title: Community and beach information - Pendine Community Council

facts.fact: Carmarthenshire Land Sailing Club was formed in 2004 to allow controlled landsailing use of Pembrey Sands and Pendine Sands, requiring £5m public liability insurance.
facts.quote: use of the beaches for landsailing, is restricted to members of carmarthenshire land sailing club, who hold the specified £5m public liability insurance, as stipulated by carmarthenshire council .

facts.fact: Any visitor could drive on Pendine beach until 2005; today driving there still costs £2,000 a day with prior permission from Carmarthenshire's local authorities.
facts.quote: until 2005, any visitor could drive on the beach - and you still can if you're prepared to pay £2000 a day and organise prior permission through carmarthenshire's local authorities .
facts.source_title: Classic shrine: Pendine Museum of Land Speed - Classic & Sports Car

facts.fact: The MOD acquired the Pendine range land in 1940 to develop WW2 weaponry and train troops for the Normandy landings; it has since been used to trial aircraft ejector seats, drone testing, and Hercules 'touch and go' landings.
facts.quote: it acquired the land in 1940 to develop ww2 weaponry and train troops for the normandy landings; it has been used more recently to trial aircraft ejector seats and for drone testing, and at one stage hercules transport aircraft performed 'touch and go' landings on the wide tracts of sand .
facts.source_title: Classic shrine: Pendine Museum of Land Speed - Classic & Sports Car

facts.fact: West of Pendine's beach lie dramatic cliffs and rock pools that were used during the Second World War for practising the D-Day landings.
facts.quote: look west and you will find dramatic cliffs with a wealth of rock pools and wild cliff top paths - this area was used during world war ii for practising the 'd-day' landings!

facts.fact: RNLI lifeguards patrol Pendine Beach daily from 11 July to 6 September in the 2026 season, 10am-6pm, with the reminder 'no flags = no lifeguards'.
facts.quote: daily 11 july - 6 september patrol times 10am-6pm

facts.fact: On Friday 15 August 2025, Tenby's RNLI inshore lifeboat was launched to assist people in the water off Pendine.
facts.quote: rescue friday 15 august 2025 tenby inshore lifeboat launched to assist people in water off pendine .

facts.fact: Natural Resources Wales' Pendine tidal flood warning area covers the Beach Hotel, post office, adjacent property, Pendine Sands Caravan Park and the A4066 coast road, with a flood warning in force as recently as 5-6 December 2025.
facts.quote: the beach hotel, post office and adjacent property, up to pendine sands caravan park, as well as the main a4066 pendine to amroth coast road
facts.source_title: Tidal area at Pendine - Flood warnings and alerts

facts.fact: Carmarthenshire County Council built the Parry Thomas Centre on Pendine promenade with five commercial premises (kayak hire, coffee, ice cream, a first-floor restaurant) after completing a traffic-free 500m promenade.
facts.quote: we firstly completed a traffic free 500m promenade and built the parry thomas commercial centre with a range of businesses ranging from kayak hire, coffee and ice cream to a hugely popular first-floor restaurant .

facts.fact: The Caban beachside accommodation and café is a two-storey, 14-bedroom purpose-built development overlooking the seven miles of Pendine sands.
facts.quote: the two storey, 14 bedroom accommodation maximises beach and sea views and is perfect for those exploring the all wales coastal park or enjoying one of the many events held on the beach such as the annual hot rods .

facts.fact: The old Pendine Museum of Speed, open since 1996 and run by Carmarthenshire County Council, received 33,522 visitors in 2009 before its 2021 demolition.
facts.quote: the museum received 33,522 visitors in 2009 .

facts.fact: The new Museum of Land Speed cost £7 million to build, decided in 2018, and Classic & Sports Car (Oct 2024) lists admission at adults £7, concessions £6, children (5-18) £4, with a 10% discount for groups of 4+.
facts.quote: how much? adults £7, concessions £6, children (5-18) £4; flexible ticket for small groups (4+) offers 10% reduction
facts.source_title: Classic shrine: Pendine Museum of Land Speed - Classic & Sports Car

recency.newest_item: A 'Babs Centenary' event is planned for Monday 27 April 2027, announced on the Pendine Community Council site (posted 13 April 2026); the most recent confirmed operational event is the RNLI's Tenby lifeboat rescue off Pendine on 15 August 2025, and a flood warning was in force for the Pendine tidal area 5-6 December 2025.

conflicts: Museum of Land Speed opening date/year: Wikipedia's Babs (car) and Owen Wyn Owen pages both say it 'was opened at pendine in 2022' [F-context, not separately fact-cited], while Wikipedia's J.G. Parry-Thomas page says the building 'was completed in early 2023 and opened on 31 march' (F-context), and Carmarthenshire Council's filming-locations page says it 'opened to the public for the first time in may 2023' (used in F42's source page). Four independent sources (council x2, Classic & Sports Car Oct 2024 'opened last year', Parry-Thomas wiki citing Western Telegraph 5 April 2023) support 2023; only the two Wikipedia car/restorer articles say 2022.

Malcolm Campbell's first Pendine record year: Carmarthenshire County Council's own business page states 'the most famous being by sir malcolm campbell in 1923 in his car blue bird' (fact F35's source page), contradicting the Wikipedia/Wikidata-sourced date of 25 September 1924 used in F03 - the council page appears to have the year wrong.

Eastern endpoint of the beach: Wikipedia's Pendine Sands article says the beach runs 'from gilman point to laugharne sands' (used in F01), while Pendine Community Council's own homepage says it stretches 'from gilman point to ginst point' - two different named eastern endpoints for the same beach.

Vehicle-ban start year: Wikipedia's Pendine Sands article says vehicles were banned '9 july 2004' to May 2010 (F14), while Wikipedia's Pendine village article says the ban ran 'between 2005 and 2010' - a one-year discrepancy on the same Wikipedia project.

Duration Babs lay buried: Wikipedia's Owen Wyn Owen page says '40 years buried on a tidal beach' (F08) and that 'in 1967, wyn owen decided to excavate,' while every other source (Pendine Sands, Babs (car), J.G. Parry-Thomas wiki pages, and Octane magazine's 2024 feature) states the car was buried for 42 years and excavated in 1969 - the Owen Wyn Owen page is the outlier.

Babs's engine power output: the Wikipedia Babs (car) infobox lists 450 bhp (F28's source), while Octane magazine's 2016/2024 factfile lists power as 'c600bhp @ 1800rpm' for the same 27-litre Liberty V12 - a large numeric discrepancy between sources.
